findings.waiverReason: F0c (Stage P4 Track F0, DEV-109): Track G's V18 migration (DEV-107) intentionally collapsed the 7-member notable* claim_type family into one canonical, which legitimately moved A10's canonical-grouping total from the frozen 835-group baseline to 798 -- a real, documented, one-time structural change, not a regression. The baseline is being re-anchored to the new figure in the same change (group_inventory_baseline.json), so this specific finding should not recur; if it does, that is a genuine new finding, not a repeat of this one. **Extended 2026-08-01 (Stage P6, DEV-148):** this waiver was written for the V18 collapse (835 -> 798) and was silently covering a second, much larger move it never anticipated — 798 -> 1,412 groups, caused by P6's re-extraction of the candidate pool (7,429 -> 9,096 rows) after the fuzzy step was demoted (DEV-143) and 63 namesake splits were registered (DEV-144/147). That is an expected re-extraction under this check's own suggested_fix, and the figure and reason are recorded in DEV-148. Recorded here so the waiver states what it actually covers. **Not covered by this waiver:** the `zero_promoted` monotonicity finding, which fired legitimately at 612 -> 1,226 because P6 re-queued 63 previously-decided rows (named in promotion_log.json under the p6-* labels); it cleared only because the check's lastZeroPromoted tracker advanced on the next run, not because the rows came back.
